Factions.Name: Lindon
Factions.Description: The Grey Havens of Lindon, last Elven realm in the west of Middle-earth: elite maritime infantry and ships, costly but disciplined, strongest given time and coast.

Technologies.Name: Harvest of the Falas
Technologies.History: The Falathrim of the Grey Havens read the tides as other men read fields, and their nets never come up empty.
Technologies.Description: Dock, Town Phase. Fishing ships +25% fish gather rate.

Technologies.Name: Elven Planning
Technologies.History: Elven halls are raised in a single day of ordered labour, as if the timber remembered its shape from Aman.
Technologies.Description: Civic Centre, Town Phase. Houses -25% build time.

Technologies.Name: Noldorin Metallurgy
Technologies.History: The Noldor of Lindon kept the metalcraft of Aman alive through the long ages, tempering blades that lesser forges cannot match.
Technologies.Description: Forge, Town Phase. Champion infantry +1 pierce attack.

Technologies.Name: Mithril-Plated Hulls
Technologies.History: The prows of Mithlond are sheathed in mithril-alloy plates, and the sea itself seems to break around them.

Technologies.Name: Elven Ladders
Technologies.History: Elven towers rise taller than any siege-ladder can reach, and their crests carry guards that never tire.
Technologies.Description: Fortress, City Phase. Fortresses and Stone Towers +15% health.

Technologies.Name: Singing Arrows
Technologies.History: The bow-strings of the Havens sing before the shafts land, and each note finds a joint in timber or stone.
Technologies.Description: Forge, City Phase. Elven Bolt-Throwers +20% pierce attack; Vanguard Saboteurs +25% crush attack.

Heroes.Name: Cirdan
Heroes.History: Cirdan the Shipwright, lord of the Falathrim and keeper of the Grey Havens since the First Age, eldest of the Elves remaining in Middle-earth. Naval hero: his ships sail faster, build sooner, and endure more near him.

Heroes.Name: Gil-galad
Heroes.History: Gil-galad, last High King of the Noldor in Middle-earth, who led the hosts of Lindon into the Last Alliance and fell facing Sauron himself. Elite commander: nearby infantry strike harder and turn aside pierce attacks.

Heroes.Name: Elrond
Heroes.History: Elrond Half-elven, herald of Gil-galad and bearer of Vilya, Ring of Air, who fought beside the High King in the War of the Last Alliance. Warrior-lord: fights with hero sword in the front line while Vilya's aura steadies nearby infantry.

CivBonuses.Name: Gift of the West
CivBonuses.History: The Elves of Lindon preserve the high craft of the Noldor, learned in Aman and refined through long ages at the Grey Havens.
CivBonuses.Description: Naval, defensive, and high-craft technologies research 15% faster (Docks, Stone Towers, Fortresses, Forges).

CivBonuses.Name: Swan Ships
CivBonuses.History: The swan-ships of the Falathrim carry the Elves along the coasts and, when need is great, bear warriors to distant shores.
CivBonuses.Description: Swan Ships carry up to 20 infantry and may train eligible Spearmaidens and Archers aboard at full cost. They provide transport and coastal reinforcement, not free troops.

CivBonuses.Name: Elven Craft
CivBonuses.History: Few in number but skilled beyond other kindreds, the warriors of Lindon favour quality over quantity.
CivBonuses.Description: Infantry favour health and discipline over numbers, with longer training times than mass-faction equivalents.

Structures.Name: Forge of the Noldor
Structures.History: The Noldor of Lindon kept the metalcraft of Aman alive through the long ages at the Grey Havens.
Structures.Description: High-craft forge. Researches Noldorin Metallurgy and Singing Arrows; its technologies complete 15% faster through the Gift of the West.

Structures.Name: Harlond
Structures.History: The sea-ward haven of Mithlond, where Cirdan the Shipwright tends the swan-ships of the Falathrim.
Structures.Description: Lindon dock. Trains Swan Ships, Fishing Boats, Merchant Ships, and Fire Galleys; repairs idle ships nearby and sharpens Mariners. Researches Harvest of the Falas and Mithril-Plated Hulls.

Structures.Name: Rider's Lodge
Structures.History: The border wardens of Mithlond ride swift horses along the shores, carrying word and warning rather than the shock of war.
Structures.Description: Light-cavalry stable. Trains Mithlond Border Riders only — no heavy cavalry, no cavalry upgrades.

Structures.Name: Works of the Havens
Structures.History: Clear-cutting forests for clunky wooden engines is antithetical to Elven culture; the Havens build slender engines that strike like needles.
Structures.Description: Elven workshop. Trains precise Bolt-Throwers for counter-siege work only — no catapults, rams, or siege towers.

Structures.Name: Arches of the Last Shore
Structures.History: A monumental archway of the West, the inland checkpoint where Elves gather before their journey across the sea.
Structures.Description: Wonder of Lindon. While the completed Arches stand, 15% of each fallen Lindon unit's cost returns to your treasury. Raze it to end the grace.
